description:

- notifyCardAssigned(params).
- notifyCommentOnCard(params).
- notifyInvited(params).

Behavior rules:
- Use only MVP types: ASSIGNED, COMMENT, INVITE.
- Self-notification guard: skip when recipientUserId === actorUserId.
- ASSIGNED: send in-app + email.
- COMMENT: notify card creator + assigned members minus commenter, dedupe recipients, in-app only.
- INVITE: create in-app notification only if invited email matches existing user account.
- linkUrl must be internal relative path generated server-side.
- Failure isolation: socket emit/email send each in their own try/catch and never rollback main mutation.

- Parent PRD: bd-2ue (Implementation order step 4)

title: PRD: In-App + Email Notification System
description:
# PRD: In-App + Email Notification System

## Problem Statement

Team members collaborating on boards have no way to know when they are assigned to cards, when someone comments on their cards, or when they are invited to a workspace — unless they manually check. The demo scenario (step 7) explicitly requires showing in-app and email notifications. The thesis requirement #3 mandates RBAC + multi-channel notifications.

## Solution

Build a notification system that delivers in-app notifications (badge + dropdown in header, full page) and email notifications (via Resend) for key collaboration events. Notifications are created as side effects of existing server actions, persisted in the Notification table, and pushed to clients in real-time via Socket.io.

## User Stories

1. As a workspace member, I want to see a notification badge in the header when I have unread notifications, so that I know something requires my attention
2. As a workspace member, I want to click the notification bell to see a dropdown of my latest notifications, so that I can quickly review what happened
3. As a workspace member, I want to click a notification to navigate to the relevant card/board, so that I can take action immediately
4. As a workspace member, I want clicked notifications to be automatically marked as read, so that my badge count stays accurate
5. As a workspace member, I want a "Mark all as read" button in the dropdown, so that I can clear multiple notifications at once
6. As a workspace member, I want to see all my notifications on a dedicated page, so that I can review older notifications
7. As a workspace member, I want to receive an email when I am assigned to a card, so that I know even when I am not using the app
8. As a workspace invitee, I want to receive an email when I am invited to a workspace, so that I can accept the invitation promptly
9. As a workspace member, I want to receive an in-app notification when I am assigned to a card, so that I see it immediately while working
10. As a workspace member, I want to receive an in-app notification when someone comments on a card I am assigned to, so that I can follow the conversation
11. As a user, I want to receive an in-app notification when I am invited to a workspace, so that I can accept without checking my email
12. As a demo presenter, I want notifications to appear in real-time via WebSocket, so that the demo shows live collaboration
13. As a demo presenter, I want the notification badge to update instantly when a notification arrives, so that the audience sees the realtime effect
14. As a developer, I want email sending to gracefully fall back to console logging when no API key is configured, so that the app works in development without Resend

## Implementation Decisions

### MVP Notification Types
- **ASSIGNED**: Created when a member is assigned to a card. Triggers in-app + email.
- **COMMENT**: Created when someone comments on a card. Notifies card creator and all assigned members (excluding the commenter). In-app only.
- **INVITE**: Created when a workspace invitation is sent. Notifies the invited user if they have an account. In-app + email.
- **MENTIONED** and **DUE_DATE** are deferred to stretch (no @mention parser exists, and DUE_DATE requires cron infrastructure).

### Architecture: Notification Service Layer
A dedicated notification service module (lib/notification.ts, marked server-only) encapsulates the full notification lifecycle. Each event-specific wrapper (notifyCardAssigned, notifyCommentOnCard, notifyInvited) performs three steps: (1) insert DB row, (2) emit Socket.io event to ROOMS.user(userId), (3) optionally send email. The service owns HOW to notify; actions own WHEN to notify.

### Failure Isolation
Socket emit and email send are wrapped in individual try/catch blocks. Failures are logged but never roll back the main mutation or the DB notification insert. The notification DB row is the durable source of truth; socket and email are best-effort enhancements.

### Self-Notification Guards
- ASSIGNED: skip when assignment.changed === false, or when recipientUserId === actorUserId
- COMMENT: exclude the commenter from recipients, deduplicate recipients
- INVITE: only create in-app notification if a User account already exists for the invited email

### Recipient Rules (Explicit)
- **ASSIGNED**: recipient = the newly assigned user. Only when changed === true. Skip if actor assigns themselves. Email: yes.
- **COMMENT**: recipients = all current card members (assigned users + card creator) minus the commenter. In-app only. If no recipients remain, no notification is created.
- **INVITE**: in-app notification only if User exists for the invited email. Email always sent via Better Auth sendInvitationEmail hook.

### Invitation Email via Better Auth Hook
Invitation emails are wired through Better Auth organization plugin's sendInvitationEmail callback in auth.ts, NOT through the generic notification service. This is because BA owns invitation creation semantics and the email link contents. The React Email invite template is reused from the notification email path. The in-app notification is still created separately in the inviteMemberAction.

### Realtime Delivery
Extend the existing Socket.io infrastructure with a new server-to-client event (notification:new) carrying the full notification payload (id, type, title, message, linkUrl, isRead, createdAt). The client-side socket listener updates the badge and dropdown in real-time. A server component baseline fetches the unread count on page load/navigation for graceful degradation when socket is disconnected.

### Notification UI
A bell icon with unread count badge is added to the authenticated header (next to the existing Invitations link). Clicking the bell opens a dropdown-menu showing the latest notifications with type-appropriate icons and timestamps. A "View all" link navigates to /notifications for the full paginated list. Clicking a notification navigates to the relevant resource (linkUrl field) and auto-marks it as read.

### Header Data Flow
AuthenticatedHeaderActions is a client component, so the unread count baseline is fetched in the server layout (app/(authenticated)/layout.tsx) and passed down as a prop to the header. This ensures the badge is accurate on every page navigation. The socket listener then updates the count in real-time between navigations.

### Email via Resend + React Email
Two React Email HTML templates: workspace invitation and card assignment. A shared email sender utility wraps the Resend SDK with a console.log fallback when RESEND_API_KEY is not set. The EMAIL_FROM address is configurable via environment variable.

### Notification Link URLs (aligned with actual routes)
- ASSIGNED: /boards/{boardId}?cardId={cardId}
- COMMENT: /boards/{boardId}?cardId={cardId}
- INVITE: /invitations
All linkUrl values are internal relative paths constructed server-side only (no user input).

### Wiring Points
- assignCardMemberAction in board actions → notifyCardAssigned
- createCommentAction in board actions → notifyCommentOnCard (notifies card members minus commenter)
- inviteMemberAction in workspace actions → notifyInvited (only if invited email has an existing user account)
- auth.ts → organization sendInvitationEmail callback for invitation emails

### Mark as Read
- Individual: auto-mark when user clicks notification (server action called on click, sets isRead=true and readAt=now)
- Bulk: "Mark all as read" button calls a server action that sets isRead=true and readAt=now for all unread notifications belonging to the user
- All read/mark queries are scoped to the session user only (never trust client-provided userId)

### Database
No schema changes needed. The Notification table and NotificationType enum already exist in the Prisma schema with all required fields (id, userId, type, title, message, linkUrl, isRead, createdAt, readAt).

### Security
- All notification read/mark actions scope by session user (userId from verifySession, never from client input)
- linkUrl values are internal relative paths only, constructed server-side
- Socket auth remains cookie-based (aligned with existing lib/realtime/auth.ts)

### Environment Variables
- RESEND_API_KEY: Resend API key for email delivery
- EMAIL_FROM: Sender address (e.g., Planora <noreply@domain.com>)

## Implementation Order

1. lib/email.ts — Resend sender utility with console fallback
2. emails/invite-email.tsx + emails/assign-email.tsx — React Email templates
3. auth.ts — wire sendInvitationEmail callback in organization plugin config
4. lib/notification.ts — notification service (create record, get unread count, list, mark read, mark all read, event-specific wrappers)
5. lib/notification-actions.ts — server actions (markRead, markAllRead)
6. lib/realtime/types.ts + events.ts + server.ts — add notification:new event + emitNotificationNew helper
7. Wire assignCardMemberAction → notifyCardAssigned
8. Wire createCommentAction → notifyCommentOnCard
9. Wire inviteMemberAction → notifyInvited
10. components/notifications/notification-bell.tsx — client component with badge + socket listener
11. components/notifications/notification-dropdown.tsx — dropdown with notification list
12. Update app/(authenticated)/layout.tsx — fetch unread count, pass to header
13. Update components/authenticated-header-actions.tsx — integrate bell
14. app/(authenticated)/(dashboard)/notifications/page.tsx — full list page
15. .env.example — add RESEND_API_KEY, EMAIL_FROM

## Testing Decisions

No test framework is configured yet. When tests are added:
- The notification service module is a deep module with a clear interface — ideal for unit testing the DB record creation, socket emission, and email sending logic independently.
- Server actions should be tested for correct notification creation after successful mutations.
- Email templates can be visually previewed using React Email preview mode.
- Mark-read actions must be tested to verify they only affect the session user's notifications.

## Out of Scope

- MENTIONED notification type (no @mention parser exists)
- DUE_DATE notification type (requires cron/scheduled job infrastructure)
- Per-user notification preferences (opt-in/out by channel or event type)
- Scheduled digest emails
- Notification sounds
- Push notifications (browser/mobile)
- Notification batching or throttling
- Email templates for comment notifications
- Cross-tab notification:read sync (acceptable staleness for MVP)
- requireEmailVerificationOnInvitation in Better Auth (consider for post-MVP)

## Further Notes

- This PRD covers thesis core requirement #3 (RBAC + multi-channel notifications).
- Demo scenario step 7 explicitly requires showing both in-app and email notifications.
- The Resend free tier (100 emails/day) is sufficient for demo purposes.
- DNS verification for the Resend domain should be completed before final demo testing.
- Email sending is fire-and-forget — failures are logged but do not block the action response.
- Socket auth is cookie-based (not JWT), consistent with the existing realtime infrastructure.
- Cross-tab read state staleness is acceptable for MVP — badge refreshes on bell open or page navigation.
